items.headline: Review Evaluates Translating Advanced Biomaterials Across Cleft Lip and Palate Care
items.preview: A narrative review highlights the uneven clinical translation of biomaterials in cleft care.
items.article:
A comprehensive narrative review evaluating clinical and preclinical literature published between 2001 and 2026 reports that while adjunctive biomaterials offer substantial therapeutic potential in cleft lip and palate management, their clinical translation remains highly uneven and predominantly preclinical. The authors determined that the primary translational barrier is not a scarcity of biomaterial functions, but an incomplete match between material design and specific surgical failure mechanisms across pediatric developmental stages.
Why this matters: Although biomaterials show measurable promise for various applications in cleft care, clinical adoption demands rigorous validation specific to the unique challenges of pediatric surgical settings. This review underscores the need for tailored approaches to enhance the effectiveness of biomaterials in clinical practice.

items.headline: Virus-like particles enable highly efficient gene editing across porcine and avian models
items.preview: Virus-like particles enhance gene editing efficiency in pigs and chickens for research applications.
items.article:
Recent advances in genome editing technologies, particularly CRISPR/Cas9, have expanded the potential of pigs and chickens as model organisms. This study evaluates virus-like particles (VLPs) as delivery vehicles for genome engineering tools in porcine and avian cultures. VLP-mediated delivery enabled efficient gene editing rates in porcine cells and robust editing in chickens, establishing VLPs as a time-saving strategy for gene editing in livestock.
Why this matters: The use of VLPs could significantly improve the efficiency of gene editing in livestock, facilitating advancements in animal health and agricultural productivity, and contributing to One Health research initiatives.

items.headline: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation
items.preview: New insights reveal how Cryptosporidium invades host cells and forms a unique interface.
items.article:
The apicomplexan parasite Cryptosporidium is a leading cause of diarrheal disease in young children. This study reveals that the single Cryptosporidium rhoptry plays a crucial role in the invasion process, acting as a conduit for effector protein secretion and ultimately forming the host-parasite interface. The findings propose a mechanistic model of Cryptosporidium invasion and intracellular parasitism.
Why this matters: Understanding the invasion mechanisms of Cryptosporidium could lead to novel therapeutic strategies to combat this significant public health threat, particularly in vulnerable populations.

items.headline: Paracetamol Fails Non-Inferiority Trial Against Meloxicam for Postoperative Canine Pain
items.preview: A trial shows paracetamol is less effective than meloxicam for pain management in dogs.
items.article:
A prospective randomized clinical trial conducted at the University of Helsinki has revealed that intravenous paracetamol does not achieve non-inferior postoperative analgesia compared to meloxicam in female dogs undergoing elective reproductive surgery. The trial established that only 40% of dogs receiving paracetamol achieved successful pain management compared to 60% in the meloxicam group.
Why this matters: The findings highlight the need for effective pain management strategies in veterinary practice, emphasizing that paracetamol cannot serve as a standalone alternative to meloxicam in postoperative care.

items.headline: A Conversation with Michael Ehlers: Funding the Future of Drug Discovery at Formation Bio
items.preview: Formation Bio discusses its new $600M fund aimed at accelerating drug development.
items.article:
Formation Bio has announced a new fund with $600M in capital commitments for in-licensing medicines and funding clinical development. The company aims to leverage AI to streamline drug discovery and development processes. Michael Ehlers, CSO and Head of R&D, emphasizes the importance of integrating data sciences with drug development to enhance efficiency and reduce costs.
Why this matters: This funding initiative represents a significant step towards accelerating the development of new therapies, potentially transforming the landscape of drug discovery and making it more efficient and accessible.
